documents.title: Rash on my wrist
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I've had an itchy, burning rash on my left wrist for about three weeks. It started after I got a new watch for the holidays. I know I react to nickel so I stopped wearing it a few days ago but it isn't going away. Could I see a dermatologist? I can send a picture.

documents.title: RE: Rash on my wrist
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry about the rash. With your nickel history that watch is a likely culprit. I've put in a dermatology referral; our front desk will call with a time. Until then keep the watch off and use a plain, unscented moisturizer. If it spreads, blisters or looks infected, let me know and I'll see you sooner.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology
Date of visit: 2024-01-16
Reason for referral: wrist rash

This is a 37-year-old woman with systemic sclerosis, a pheochromocytoma and known nickel sensitivity. About three weeks ago an itchy rash appeared on her left wrist shortly after she began wearing a new wristwatch. She took the watch off three days ago but the rash has not settled. No change in laundry products or soap. She does dab perfume on both wrists most days. The area itches and burns. She feels otherwise well.

Medications: phenoxybenzamine 10 mg BID, atenolol 50 mg daily (since last summer), amlodipine 10 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, sildenafil 20 mg TID, omeprazole 20 mg.
Allergies: nickel - contact dermatitis.

Exam: Eczematous, itchy plaque on the left wrist in the footprint of the watch back and band, with burning on palpation. No eruption elsewhere. No systemic signs.

Assessment: Allergic contact dermatitis of the left wrist from nickel in the watch. Fragrance applied to the same site is a probable additional contact allergen; we have added fragrance to her allergy list.

Plan:
1. Triamcinolone 0.1% cream to the wrist twice daily for two weeks, then stop.
2. Avoid nickel against the skin; a coat of clear nail polish on metal backs, or a nickel-free band.
3. Fragrance-free soaps, lotions and no perfume on the skin.
4. Return as needed.
Dermatology

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: heavy periods.

Cycles have been irregular since last fall (noted at endo in October). The last three have been very heavy - changing a super pad every 1-2 hours on the worst days, passing clots, 8-9 days long. Missed a day of work last month. No bleeding between, no pain beyond usual cramps. Some fatigue, though she has had that since fall.

Wrist rash cleared with the dermatology cream; she's using a nickel-free band and no perfume.

BP OK today. Pale? No. Abd soft, nontender. Pelvic deferred - will be done by gyn.

A/P
1. Menorrhagia with irregular cycles. CBC today. Referral to gynecology. She wants to talk about all options, including surgery.
2. Contact dermatitis - resolved.
3. Pheo/secondary HTN - continue meds.

documents.title: CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin and platelets in normal range despite the bleeding. Portal message sent. Gyn appt pending.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology group
Annual visit, 2024-04-08

Since last year she was diagnosed with a pheochromocytoma (endocrinology) and has had a nickel/fragrance contact dermatitis of the wrist, now cleared. She is seeing gynecology soon about heavy menses.
Skin thickening of hands, forearms and anterior chest: unchanged. No ulcers. Joints quiet.
BP 136/84 in clinic on her current regimen. Your recent creatinine normal.
Medications as per your list, including phenoxybenzamine and atenolol.
Impression: diffuse cutaneous SSc, stable.
Plan: no change. Continue close BP and kidney monitoring. Return in one year.
Rheumatology

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside gynecology
Seen 2024-04-22

37-year-old G0 referred for heavy menstrual bleeding with irregular cycles for about six months. Background: diffuse systemic sclerosis, SSc-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension, pheochromocytoma on alpha and beta blockade.
She describes heavy, prolonged, clotty bleeding that is disrupting work. Does not desire future fertility and has thought about this for some time.
Exam: unremarkable abdominal exam. Pelvic exam without abnormality on today's examination.
We discussed medical options and surgery. She would like definitive treatment and chooses total abdominal hysterectomy. Risks reviewed, including bleeding, infection, and injury to bowel, bladder or ureters.
I spoke with her endocrinologist, who is comfortable with surgery on her current phenoxybenzamine and atenolol, and with her pulmonary hypertension cardiologist regarding anesthesia planning.
Plan: total abdominal hysterectomy, to be scheduled for July.
Gynecology

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Indication: lower abdominal pain, postoperative day 1 after total abdominal hysterectomy.
Technique: axial images of the abdomen and pelvis after intravenous contrast.
Findings: Large volume of free fluid in the peritoneal cavity. No dilated or thickened bowel loops, no free intraperitoneal air beyond expected postoperative change, no bowel wall discontinuity. No organized or rim-enhancing collection. Postsurgical changes of hysterectomy at the vaginal cuff. Liver, spleen and pancreas unremarkable. Kidneys enhance symmetrically.
reports.conclusion: Large-volume peritoneal fluid after hysterectomy. No evidence of bowel injury or intra-abdominal abscess.

documents.title: Gynecology Discharge Summary
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Area hospital - gynecology inpatient service
Admitted: 2024-07-16   Discharged: 2024-07-22
Procedure: total abdominal hysterectomy (2024-07-16) for menorrhagia
Allergies: nickel; fragrances

Hospital course:
Surgery on 7/16 was completed as planned. Phenoxybenzamine and atenolol were continued perioperatively at endocrinology's direction.
About twelve hours after surgery she developed constant lower abdominal pain that did not radiate. She had no nausea or vomiting and no change in bowel function. On POD 1 (7/17): BP 130/85, HR 90, T 37.2 C. Abdomen mildly distended and diffusely tender without rebound or guarding; no CVA tenderness. Urine output had been normal since the operation. Labs: hemoglobin 12.5, WBC 11.0, creatinine 0.9, BUN 14; urinalysis normal without blood or pyuria.
CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast showed a large amount of peritoneal fluid without bowel injury or abscess.
Given the volume of fluid, urology was consulted. Cystoscopy with left retrograde study on 7/18 showed contrast extravasation from the left distal ureter, consistent with an operative laceration. A left ureteral stent was placed. Pain improved over the following days, she tolerated diet, ambulated and voided normally around the stent. Pain controlled with oral analgesics in hospital.

Discharge diagnoses: s/p total abdominal hysterectomy for menorrhagia; iatrogenic left ureteral laceration, stented.
Discharge medications: unchanged home medications (phenoxybenzamine 10 mg BID, atenolol 50 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, sildenafil 20 mg TID, omeprazole 20 mg daily). [Hydrochlorothiazide not listed on our medication reconciliation.]
Follow-up: urology in about 6 weeks for stent removal; gynecology wound check 2 weeks; PCP within 1 week.
Gynecology

documents.title: Post-discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call 2 business days after discharge. Home since 7/22. Pain improving, using what the hospital told her. Voiding OK with some urgency from the stent. Incision dry. Has urology f/u being scheduled. Taking all her BP meds including HCTZ - she noticed it was missing from the discharge list and asked; told her to continue as before, will confirm at visit. Appt 7/29.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Discharge summary reviewed. TAH 7/16 for menorrhagia; POD1 lower abdominal pain, CT with lots of peritoneal fluid but no bowel injury; urology found a left distal ureteral laceration on retrograde study and placed a stent 7/18. Home 7/22.

Now: pain mild and steadily better. Some urinary urgency and a little flank twinge when voiding - typical stent symptoms. No fever. Eating normally.

Meds reconciled - HCTZ dropped off their list in error, she has been taking it; continued. Otherwise same 7 meds.

BP 132/84, afebrile. Incision clean, dry, intact, no erythema. Abd soft, appropriately tender near incision. No CVA tenderness.

A/P
1. S/p TAH - menorrhagia resolved. No further cervical screening needed (benign indication, cervix removed).
2. Iatrogenic L ureteral injury, stented - urology to remove stent ~6 wks. Creatinine checked today.
3. Secondary HTN/pheo - at goal-ish, continue.
Call with fever, worsening flank pain or reduced urine.

documents.title: BMP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine 0.9, same as in hospital. Good.

documents.title: Urology Procedure Letter
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology
Date: 2024-09-05
Procedure: cystoscopy with removal of left ureteral stent

Seven weeks after stent placement for an intraoperative left distal ureteral laceration during hysterectomy. She has had only mild stent irritation. Office cystoscopy, stent grasped and removed intact without difficulty. Tolerated well. Voided afterward without trouble.
Plan: renal ultrasound in about 6 weeks to make sure there is no hydronephrosis. Call with fever, flank pain or poor urine output.
Urology

reports.text:
Indication: follow-up after left ureteral stent removal.
Right kidney 10.9 cm, left kidney 11.1 cm, normal cortical thickness and echogenicity. No hydronephrosis on either side. No stones or masses. Bladder adequately distended, unremarkable.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
38F annual.

Year in review: TAH in July for menorrhagia, complicated by L ureteral laceration - stented, stent out 9/5, renal US normal 10/14. Fully recovered, back at work since late August. Wrist dermatitis cleared in the winter. Pheo on phenoxybenzamine/atenolol; spells rare. Rheum stable in April.
Breathing - about the same, maybe a little more winded on the stairs at work lately; PH clinic visit is due in January.
Mood good, PHQ-2 0.

Meds: phenoxybenzamine 10 BID, atenolol 50, amlodipine 10, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, sildenafil 20 TID, omeprazole 20. Allergies: nickel, fragrance.

Exam: BP 134/84. Well. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd: healed lower abdominal incision, nontender. Skin: SSc changes unchanged. No edema.

A/P
- Health maintenance: flu done Oct; updated COVID today. No Paps needed post-TAH. Mammogram discussion at 40.
- Chronic problems stable; labs today.
- Keep the January PH appointment and mention the stairs.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Lungs clear without infiltrate, effusion or pneumothorax. Cardiomediastinal silhouette within normal limits. No structural abnormality of the bony thorax.

Right atrium and right ventricle are enlarged. Left ventricle normal in size with normal systolic function. Left atrium normal. No significant valvular abnormality on this study. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Right-sided chamber enlargement with preserved left ventricular size and function.

reports.text: Pulmonary function testing performed with acceptable and reproducible efforts. Spirometry, lung volumes and diffusing capacity within normal limits for age, sex and height.
Sinus rhythm. Right axis deviation. Nonspecific ST-T wave changes.
reports.conclusion: Right axis deviation; nonspecific ST-T changes.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology - pulmonary hypertension program
Visit: 2025-01-20

Reason: scheduled follow-up of systemic sclerosis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension.

Over the past several months she has become steadily more short of breath with exertion - stairs and hills now wind her - and now and then has a dull chest discomfort while exerting. Her ankles are a little puffy by evening. She has no orthopnea, no paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea and no recent infections.
She also mentions that her fingers sometimes change color in the cold; she has never had this looked at.
Social: no tobacco, no recreational drugs.
Medications: sildenafil 20 mg TID, phenoxybenzamine 10 mg BID, atenolol 50 mg, amlodipine 10 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, omeprazole 20 mg. Allergies: nickel, fragrances.

Exam: BP 126/78, HR 78, SpO2 97% - all within normal limits. Prominent, loud P2. Trace edema at both ankles. No rales or wheezes. No murmurs.

Studies today:
- Chest radiograph: no infiltrate or structural abnormality.
- Echocardiogram: enlarged right atrium and ventricle; LV size and function preserved.
- PFTs: unremarkable.
- ECG: right axis deviation, nonspecific ST-T changes.

Impression:
1. Progression of SSc-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension, now with right heart enlargement and exertional symptoms.
2. Cold-induced digital color change consistent with Raynaud phenomenon.

Plan: continue sildenafil 20 mg three times daily. Return in 6 months.
Cardiology

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after the January PH clinic letter: worsening exertional breathlessness, right heart now enlarged on echo, loud P2, trace ankle edema; PFTs and CXR normal; ECG right axis. Cardiology kept sildenafil the same, recheck in 6 months.

She says stairs at work are harder; she takes the elevator now. Ankles a bit puffy at night. Fingers go white then blue in the cold - this winter she noticed it more; she never thought to mention it before.

BP 136/86. SpO2 normal. Loud P2. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema both sides. Fingers warm today.

A/P
1. SSc-PAH, progressing per cardiology - their plan. Return precautions: syncope, chest pain at rest, rapid weight gain.
2. Raynaud phenomenon - added to our problem list. Gloves, keep core warm.
3. Secondary HTN/pheo - continue regimen. BMP today.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology group
Visit 2025-04-14

Annual review. The PH team found progression of her pulmonary arterial hypertension in January and documented Raynaud phenomenon. Today: skin thickening of the hands, forearms and chest without change. Fingers warm in clinic, no ulcers or pits. Joints without synovitis.
BP 134/84.
Impression: diffuse cutaneous SSc, skin stable; PAH per cardiology; Raynaud phenomenon.
Plan: cold avoidance and gloves. No new treatment from rheumatology. Continue BP and creatinine checks with PCP; same-day call for any sudden BP rise or headache. One year.
Rheumatology

documents.title: Dermatology Telehealth Visit
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology - video visit
Date: 2025-07-28

39-year-old with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis and nickel contact allergy, seen by video for a left wrist rash that has recurred over three weeks, much like her January 2024 episode. Again it began soon after she started wearing a new wristwatch, which she removed three days ago without improvement. No change in detergent or soap; she still often puts perfume on her wrists.
Allergies: nickel, fragrances.
Exam by video, with photos uploaded through the portal: itchy, eczematous patch at the left wrist where the watch sat; she reports burning. Nothing elsewhere. No systemic features.
Assessment: recurrent allergic contact dermatitis, left wrist, nickel with likely fragrance contribution.
Plan: triamcinolone 0.1% cream twice daily for two weeks. Strict nickel avoidance - a dimethylglyoxime spot test kit can check jewelry. Stop perfume on the skin. Follow up as needed.
Dermatology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
39F annual. Rescheduled BP visit from May never happened, so catching up.

Wrist rash came back in July with another watch; derm video visit, steroid cream, cleared by mid-August. No perfume now, tests her jewelry.
PH clinic in January found progression; still on sildenafil alone. Exertional breathlessness about the same as in winter. Ankles puffy some evenings. Raynaud in the cold, gloves help.
Pheo spells: maybe once a month, brief.
PHQ-2 1. Work going OK.

Meds: phenoxybenzamine 10 BID, atenolol 50, amlodipine 10, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, sildenafil 20 TID, omeprazole 20. Allergies: nickel, fragrance.

Exam: BP 136/84. Loud P2, regular. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema. Skin: SSc changes stable; wrist clear.

A/P
- Contact dermatitis: resolved.
- PAH/SSc/pheo/HTN: continue, specialists following.
- Prevention: flu and COVID done 10/6. Turns 40 in June - screening mammogram then.
- Labs today. RTC 3 months.
